title: Venous thromboembolism (DVT / PE)
subtitle: Diagnose with pretest probability → D-dimer → imaging · triage PE by ESC risk class · 3 months for everyone, then stop for a major transient provocation or extend (often reduced-dose DOAC) for unprovoked or persistent risk · DOACs first-line; LMWH or warfarin in pregnancy, APS and selected cancers
source: Compiled from the Fellowship DVT/PE, Anticoagulation & Reversal and Hematology in Pregnancy reviews · ESC 2019 PE, ASH 2018–2021, ASCO 2023, ISTH SSC guidance · FDA labels · primary trial reports verified against published abstracts, October 2026.

blocks.heading: Diagnosis
items: Pretest probability first. Wells DVT ≤1 → D-dimer (negative excludes), ≥2 → compression ultrasound. Wells PE ≤4 → D-dimer, >4 → CTPA
PERC only if gestalt <15%: age <50, HR <100, SaO₂ ≥95%, no hemoptysis, estrogen, prior VTE, leg swelling, recent surgery/trauma → no testing
Age-adjusted D-dimer: age × 10 µg/L if >50 y ADJUST-PE. YEARS: no items (DVT signs, hemoptysis, PE most likely) → exclude if <1000 ng/mL; ≥1 item → <500; CTPA avoided in 48%
D-dimer rules out, never in — skip it when probability is high
Imaging: CUS (repeat in 1 wk if negative proximal scan + high suspicion). CTPA for PE; V/Q if contrast allergy, renal failure, or pregnancy with normal CXR. Unstable: bedside echo + CUS

blocks.heading: Acute PE risk — ESC 2019
rows: Hemodynamic instability: arrest, SBP <90 or pressors, or SBP drop ≥40 for >15 min
UFH + systemic lysis; embolectomy (surgical/catheter) if contraindicated or fails
Anticoagulate, monitor; rescue lysis or catheter therapy if decompensates; PERT
sPESI ≥1 + one or neither, or sPESI 0 + either positive
blocks.footnote: sPESI (1 each): age >80, cancer, chronic heart/lung disease, HR ≥110, SBP <100, SaO₂ <90%. RV dysfunction: RV/LV ≥1.0 on CT or echo dilation/hypokinesis. Hestia: 11 exclusions (O₂ need, bleeding risk, CrCl <30, pregnancy, social…).

blocks.heading: Acute PE — therapies
items: Systemic lysis for high-risk PE only: alteplase 100 mg over 2 h. Not routine in intermediate-high: tenecteplase cut decompensation 2.6% vs 5.6% but hemorrhagic stroke 2.0% vs 0.2% PEITHO
Catheter-directed therapy: lysis contraindicated, or intermediate-high deteriorating — PERT decision. UFH first if lysis/procedure likely
IVC filter only if acute proximal DVT/PE + anticoagulation contraindicated; retrievable — anticoagulate and remove once safe. Not for recurrence on therapy or added to anticoagulation

blocks.heading: Provoked vs unprovoked — ISTH 2016 / ESC 2019
rows: Surgery >30 min general anesthesia; bed-bound admission ≥3 d; cesarean; major trauma
Short surgery or admission; estrogen, pregnancy; leg injury; long-haul travel
blocks.footnote: Recurrence after stopping, first unprovoked VTE: 10% at 1 y, 25% at 5 y, 36% at 10 y; higher in men Khan BMJ 2019. Age-appropriate cancer screening only.

boxes: extend only if the risk persists
extended, no stop date if bleeding risk
full dose if recurrence on reduced dose (RENOVE:
reduced dose missed NI, but less bleeding)
aspirin only if stopping: ~32% fewer recurrences

blocks.heading: Extended-phase evidence
items: Apixaban 2.5 or 5 mg BID vs placebo: recurrence 1.7% / 1.7% vs 8.8%, no increase in major bleeding AMPLIFY-EXT
Rivaroxaban 10 or 20 mg vs aspirin 100 mg: 1.2% / 1.5% vs 4.4% EINSTEIN-CHOICE
Higher recurrence risk: male sex, proximal DVT or PE (vs distal), D-dimer high after stopping, obesity, APS, active cancer

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — choosing the agent, cancer, special populations, unusual sites, thrombophilia

blocks.heading: Choosing the anticoagulant
rows: Default; no lead-in; ~27% renal — best DOAC in CKD and GI cancer; major bleeding RR 0.31 vs LMWH/warfarin (AMPLIFY)
Lysis likely; CrCl <30; high bleeding risk

blocks.heading: Cancer-associated VTE — ASCO 2023, ASH 2021
items: DOAC or LMWH ≥6 mo, then while cancer is active. Treat incidental clot like symptomatic

DOACs cut recurrence vs dalteparin; edoxaban/rivaroxaban add GI/GU bleeding: edoxaban major bleeding 6.9% vs 4.0% (Hokusai); rivaroxaban recurrence 4% vs 11%, CRNMB 13% vs 4% (SELECT-D). Apixaban no excess: 3.8% vs 4.0% (Caravaggio), 0% vs 1.4% (ADAM VTE)
LMWH (or apixaban) for unresected luminal GI/GU tumors, platelets <50k, poor intake, interacting drugs (enzalutamide, apalutamide, azoles, ritonavir)
Extended: apixaban 2.5 mg BID after ≥6 mo — recurrence 2.1% vs 2.8%, bleeding 12.1% vs 15.6% API-CAT

Prophylaxis: starting chemo + Khorana ≥2 + low bleeding risk → apixaban 2.5 BID or rivaroxaban 10 daily. AVERT 4.2% vs 10.2%; CASSINI NS at 180 d (6.0% vs 8.8%). Myeloma + IMiD: aspirin or LMWH/DOAC by risk

blocks.heading: Khorana score
rows: High-risk site: lung, lymphoma, gynecologic, bladder, testicular
Pre-chemo platelets ≥350k · Hb <10 or ESA · WBC >11k · BMI ≥35
blocks.footnote: 0 low, 1–2 intermediate, ≥3 high. Trials and ASCO 2023 use ≥2 as the prophylaxis threshold.

blocks.heading: Special populations
rows: Warfarin INR 2–3; no DOACs, above all triple-positive or arterial events. TRAPS (rivaroxaban, triple-positive): thromboembolism 12% vs 0, stopped early; ASTRO-APS (apixaban): excess strokes

Therapeutic LMWH by weight; no routine anti-Xa. No warfarin or DOAC antepartum. Treat to ≥6 wk postpartum, ≥3 mo total. Planned delivery: last therapeutic dose 24 h before neuraxial (prophylactic 12 h). Postpartum LMWH or warfarin (breastfeeding OK); DOAC only if not breastfeeding
Antepartum prophylaxis if prior VTE was unprovoked or hormonal; postpartum prophylaxis 6 wk for most. Fixed low-dose LMWH is enough — weight-adjusted intermediate dose no better (Highlow: 2% vs 3%)
Standard-dose apixaban or rivaroxaban at any BMI/weight (ISTH 2021); avoid dabigatran/edoxaban at extremes; no routine DOAC levels. After bariatric surgery: parenteral first, not a DOAC
CrCl <30: apixaban (limited data), UFH, or enoxaparin 1 mg/kg daily; avoid dabigatran (≤30) and rivaroxaban (<15); edoxaban 30 mg for CrCl 15–50. Dialysis: apixaban or warfarin
>50k: full dose. 25–50k: acute, high-risk clot → full-dose LMWH + platelet transfusion to 40–50k; otherwise 50% or prophylactic LMWH. <25k: hold ISTH 2018. Avoid DOACs <50k

Stop all heparin (flushes too); argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux or a DOAC. No warfarin until platelets recover (≥150k), then overlap ≥5 d; vitamin K if on warfarin at diagnosis. Bilateral CUS. With thrombosis treat 3 mo
DOAC over warfarin; apixaban lowest bleeding. AF dose-reduction criteria do not apply to VTE — apixaban 5 mg BID regardless of age/weight/creatinine

Confirm it is new clot (compare with baseline imaging). Check adherence, dose, interactions, absorption; look for cancer, APS, HIT, MPN/PNH, May-Thurner. DOAC/warfarin → therapeutic LMWH; on LMWH → raise dose 20–25%

blocks.heading: Recurrence and bleeding risk
items: HERDOO2 (women, first unprovoked VTE, after 5–12 mo): post-thrombotic signs, D-dimer ≥250 µg/L on treatment, BMI ≥30, age ≥65. ≤1 → may stop: 3.0%/pt-yr vs 8.1% in high-risk women + men REVERSE II
Bleeding risk: age >65–75, prior bleeding, cancer, renal/liver failure, low platelets, prior stroke, antiplatelets, alcohol, anemia → high risk favors stopping at 3 mo

blocks.heading: Unusual sites and distal clot
rows: Non-cirrhotic: JAK2 V617F (then CALR, marrow), PNH flow, APS; local causes. Treat ≥3–6 mo; indefinite if MPN, unprovoked, Budd-Chiari. Screen varices without delaying
Anticoagulate even with hemorrhagic infarct. Heparin → DOAC acceptable (RE-SPECT CVT, n=120; ACTION-CVT cohort: less major hemorrhage, HR 0.35). 3–12 mo
3 mo or while the line stays; keep a working, needed line. Paget-Schroetter: CDT + thoracic outlet decompression
≥5 cm, >3 cm from SFJ → fondaparinux 2.5 mg ×45 d (CALISTO 0.9% vs 5.9%). ≤3 cm from SFJ → treat as DVT
Mild, no risk factors → serial CUS over 2 wk. Treat 3 mo if severe symptoms, extensive, cancer, inpatient, prior VTE. CACTUS: nadroparin no better (3% vs 5%), bleeding 4% vs 0%

blocks.heading: Thrombophilia testing
items: Don't test if it won't change management: major transient provocation; unprovoked VTE already on extended therapy; cancer; acute clot or on anticoagulation; routine relatives

May matter: APS in young unprovoked VTE, unusual sites, arterial + venous events, pregnancy morbidity — before choosing a DOAC. Women with a relative's VTE + known thrombophilia weighing estrogen/pregnancy

Timing: FVL, PT G20210A any time. Protein C/S, AT fall with acute clot; warfarin lowers C/S, heparin AT, pregnancy S; DOACs falsely raise clot-based assays. LA unreliable on DOAC/warfarin; ELISAs unaffected. APS needs persistence ≥12 wk

blocks.heading: Thrombophilias
headers: Prevalence · RR first VTE ASH Ed 2016
rows: APC resistance; ~20% of VTE pts. Homozygous much higher
Free S low in pregnancy, estrogen
APS, cancer, MPN (JAK2), PNH, nephrotic syndrome, IBD, HIT, estrogen, pregnancy

blocks.heading: Agents — dosing
rows: 2.5 mg BID after ≥6 mo. No renal or age reduction for VTE
15 mg BID ×21 d → 20 mg daily, with food
10 mg daily after ≥6 mo. Avoid CrCl <15
30 mg if CrCl 15–50, ≤60 kg, or P-gp inhibitor
Start with parenteral; overlap ≥5 d and until INR ≥2 for 24 h; target 2–3
1 mg/kg q12h (1.5 mg/kg daily option; avoid in obesity/cancer)
CrCl <30: 1 mg/kg daily. Peak anti-Xa 0.6–1.0 (q12h) if obese, pregnant, renal
Cancer: 200 IU/kg daily ×1 mo → 150 IU/kg daily (max 18,000 IU)
<50 kg 5 mg · 50–100 kg 7.5 mg · >100 kg 10 mg daily
Preferred for CrCl <30 or likely lysis
2 µg/kg/min (0.5–1.2 if hepatic dysfunction, ICU); aPTT 1.5–3× baseline
Hold UFH during infusion (US label); ESC allows continuing

blocks.heading: Switching agents
rows: Give DOAC when the next LMWH dose is due
Start DOAC when the infusion stops
Start when the next DOAC dose is due
Stop warfarin; start apixaban/dabigatran at INR <2, edoxaban ≤2.5, rivaroxaban <3
Overlap until INR ≥2 (edoxaban: halve dose during overlap); DOACs raise the INR — draw at DOAC trough

blocks.heading: Follow-up after VTE
items: Post-thrombotic syndrome (pain, swelling, skin change, ulcer; score by Villalta): stockings do not prevent it — 14.2% vs 12.7% with placebo stockings SOX 2014; use them for symptoms. No routine catheter lysis for proximal DVT: PTS 47% vs 48%, major bleeding 1.7% vs 0.3% ATTRACT 2017
CTEPH: persistent dyspnea or exercise limitation at 3–6 mo after PE → echo + V/Q scan (more sensitive than CTPA for chronic clot) → CTEPH center. No routine screening of asymptomatic patients
At 3 months: recheck bleeding risk, renal function, CBC, adherence; record a baseline CUS/imaging if it would help judge a future recurrence

blocks.heading: Periprocedural management
items: DOACs: hold by bleeding risk, no bridging, no pre-op levels PAUSE 2019. Xa inhibitors: low/moderate risk skip 1 day before, resume day 1 after; high risk skip 2 days, resume day 2–3. Dabigatran with CrCl <50: 2 d / 4 d. Major bleeding ≤2% (~3% high-risk procedures), arterial events <1% (AF population)
Warfarin: stop 5 d before; no bridging for most — BRIDGE (AF): arterial events 0.4% vs 0.3%, major bleeding 1.3% vs 3.2% with LMWH bridging
VTE <3 months ago: defer elective surgery; if it can't wait, bridge with LMWH; if <1 mo and surgery is mandatory, a retrievable filter can be considered
Neuraxial: follow ASRA intervals; prophylactic LMWH 12 h, therapeutic 24 h before the needle

blocks.heading: Drug interactions
items: Avoid DOACs with strong combined CYP3A4 + P-gp inducers: rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort, enzalutamide, apalutamide → use LMWH

Strong combined inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir incl. nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, cobicistat): avoid rivaroxaban; apixaban halve the dose (avoid if already on 2.5 mg). Dabigatran/edoxaban: P-gp inhibitors (dronedarone, ketoconazole) raise levels
Bleeding add-ons: antiplatelets, NSAIDs, SSRIs, ibrutinib; stop aspirin unless there is a firm arterial indication

blocks.heading: Hormonal therapy — VTE risk by type
rows: ↑ ~3× (OR 2.97): levonorgestrel / norethisterone / norgestimate ~2.5×; desogestrel, gestodene, drospirenone, cyproterone ~3.6–4.3× Vinogradova BMJ 2015
↑ ~8× patch, ~6.5× ring vs non-users; ~2× vs levonorgestrel pill Lidegaard BMJ 2012
↑ ~1.6× (hepatic first pass); CEE + MPA 2.1×, estradiol + dydrogesterone 1.2× (NS)
No ↑ (OR 0.93 Vinogradova BMJ 2019; 0.9 ESTHER) — preferred; pair with micronized progesterone or dydrogesterone
blocks.footnote: Low-dose vaginal estrogen: no clear ↑. Estrogen-containing or progestin-only therapy may continue during therapeutic anticoagulation (no excess recurrence, EINSTEIN — Martinelli Blood 2016); stop estrogen before anticoagulation ends (German guidance: ≥6 wk before). Gender-affirming: estradiol not ethinyl estradiol; transdermal preferred.

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Apixaban 2.5 or 5 mg BID vs placebo, 12 mo after 6–12 mo Rx: recurrent VTE/VTE death 1.7% / 1.7% vs 8.8%; major bleeding 0.2 / 0.1 vs 0.5%
Rivaroxaban 20 / 10 mg vs aspirin 100 mg (n=3396): recurrence 1.5% / 1.2% vs 4.4%; no significant bleeding increase
High-risk, reduced vs full-dose DOAC (n=2768): recurrence 2.2% vs 1.8%, noninferiority not met; clinically relevant bleeding 9.9% vs 15.2%
Edoxaban vs dalteparin: recurrence/major bleeding 12.8% vs 13.5% (NI); major bleeding 6.9% vs 4.0%, mostly GI cancer
Rivaroxaban vs dalteparin (n=406): 6-mo recurrence 4% vs 11%; CRNMB 13% vs 4%
Apixaban vs dalteparin (n=1155): recurrence 5.6% vs 7.9% (NI); major bleeding 3.8% vs 4.0%
Cancer, after ≥6 mo: apixaban 2.5 vs 5 mg BID (n=1766): recurrence 2.1% vs 2.8% (NI); CR bleeding 12.1% vs 15.6%
Apixaban vs dalteparin (n=300): major bleeding 0% vs 1.4% (NS); recurrence 0.7% vs 6.3%
Khorana ≥2, apixaban 2.5 BID vs placebo: VTE 4.2% vs 10.2%; major bleeding 3.5% on apixaban
Rivaroxaban 10 mg vs placebo: 6.0% vs 8.8% at 180 d (NS); on-treatment 2.6% vs 6.4%
Triple-positive APS: rivaroxaban thromboembolism 12% vs 0 on warfarin → stopped early, no DOACs
Intermediate-risk PE, tenecteplase: death/decompensation 2.6% vs 5.6%; hemorrhagic stroke 2.0% vs 0.2% → no routine lysis
Variable D-dimer threshold: CTPA avoided in 48% of suspected PE
SVT ≥5 cm, fondaparinux 2.5 mg ×45 d: 0.9% vs 5.9%
Low-risk calf DVT: nadroparin vs placebo 3% vs 5% (NS); bleeding 4% vs 0%
Pregnancy, prior VTE: weight-adjusted intermediate vs fixed low-dose LMWH, VTE 2% vs 3% (NS) → low dose
Stockings and catheter lysis do not prevent PTS; ATTRACT more major bleeding
Standardized DOAC holds, no bridging: major bleeding ≤2% (~3% high-risk procedures), arterial <1%. Bridging warfarin raised major bleeding 1.3% → 3.2%, no fewer arterial events
